newsitem.title: HUNGARY: Hungary's forint firms vs dollar, steady vs basket.
newsitem.headline: Hungary's forint firms vs dollar, steady vs basket.

text.p: Hungary's forint closed firmer against the dollar and steady versus the central bank basket, with increased demand for the forint due to a 10 basis point cut in the monthly devaluation rate on Friday, dealers said.
The Hungarian forint traded pinned to the NBH's resistance level (bid) and finished the morning session at 197.85/90, compared with the opening 198.05/10.

Demand for the forint has been strengthened by the reduction of the monthly crawling peg devaluation rate to one percent from 1.1 percent, as the cut made forint interest rates more attractive compared with foreign currency interest rates, traders said.
"The reduction of the devaluation rate has made the forint more attractive," said Mihaly Donka of BNP-Dredner Bank. The offers were at the National Bank of Hungary's (NBH) bid,"
Traders said almost all market players were foreign currency sellers in the past few days, pushing the forint to the top of the 4.5 percent wide NBH intervention range.
